title: The future subjunctive and other fossils
summary: The future subjunctive (hablare, fuere, hubiere) and other relics of formal Spanish: where they survive, what they mean today and how to read them.
focus: Recognising the future subjunctive and archaic formulas in legal, proverbial and literary prose
content:
## A future built on the preterite

The **futuro de subjuntivo** takes the stem of the preterite *ellos* form (the same stem as **hablara / hablase**) and adds **-re**: **hablaron → hablare**, **tuvieron → tuviere**.

| | hablar | tener | ser / ir | haber |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | hablare | tuviere | fuere | hubiere |
| tú | hablares | tuvieres | fueres | hubieres |
| él / ella / usted | hablare | tuviere | fuere | hubiere |
| nosotros/as | habláremos | tuviéremos | fuéremos | hubiéremos |
| vosotros/as | hablareis | tuviereis | fuereis | hubiereis |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | hablaren | tuvieren | fueren | hubieren |

Only **nosotros** carries a written accent, so **hablare** is not the future **hablaré**. Likewise **hacer → hiciere**, **venir → viniere**, **ver → viere**.

## Where it survives

Everyday Spanish dropped it centuries ago. You meet it in three places:

- **Laws, contracts and rulebooks**, especially older codes still in force: *El que hiciere uso indebido del sello será sancionado.* (Anyone who misuses the seal shall be penalised.) *Si no hubiere quórum, se levantará la sesión.* (Should there be no quorum, the meeting shall be adjourned.)
- **Proverbs and set phrases**: **adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres** (when in Rome, do as the Romans do), **sea lo que fuere** (be that as it may), **venga lo que viniere** (come what may).
- **Deliberately archaic or mock-solemn writing**, where it sounds like a notary reading out a deed.

## Reading it: the modern equivalents

Recognise it, but do not produce it. To read a fossil, swap in a present form:

| fossil | modern | rule |
|---|---|---|
| si no hubiere acuerdo | si no **hay** acuerdo | after **si**: present indicative |
| el que hiciere trampa | el que **haga** trampa | relative clause: present subjunctive |
| cuando llegare el plazo | cuando **llegue** el plazo | time clause: present subjunctive |
| sea lo que fuere | sea lo que **sea** | set phrase: present subjunctive |
| adonde fueres | adonde **vayas** | present subjunctive |

In a work e-mail, **si tuviere alguna duda** sounds like a deed from another century: write **si tiene alguna duda**.

## Other fossils of formal prose

- **Pronouns stuck to a finite verb**: **díjole** = *le dijo*; **érase una vez** = *había una vez* (once upon a time); **hízose el silencio** = *se hizo el silencio*. Today: fairy tales, parody, very literary prose.
- **so pena de** (on pain of; *so* is the old word for *bajo*): *so pena de multa*.
- **a la sazón** (at that time): *el ministro, a la sazón embajador en Lima, …*
- **otrora** (formerly, once): *la otrora próspera ciudad*.
- **el susodicho / la susodicha** (the aforementioned): legal, but often ironic in speech: *Y entonces apareció la susodicha.*

vocabulary.meaning: future subjunctive of hablar (legal, archaic; today hable)
vocabulary.example: El testigo que hablare sin permiso será amonestado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Any witness who speaks without permission shall be warned.

vocabulary.meaning: future subjunctive of ser / ir (today sea / vaya)
vocabulary.example: Si el acusado fuere menor de edad, se aplicará la ley especial.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Should the accused be a minor, the special law shall apply.

vocabulary.meaning: future subjunctive of haber (today haya / hay)
vocabulary.example: Si no hubiere herederos, los bienes pasarán al Estado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Should there be no heirs, the property shall pass to the State.

vocabulary.example: El que hiciere trampa perderá la fianza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Whoever cheats shall forfeit the deposit.

vocabulary.example: Quien tuviere noticia del hecho deberá comunicarlo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Anyone who has knowledge of the event must report it.

vocabulary.meaning: be that as it may, whatever it is (today sea lo que sea)
vocabulary.example: Sea lo que fuere, el contrato ya está firmado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Be that as it may, the contract is already signed.

vocabulary.meaning: come what may (today venga lo que venga)
vocabulary.example: Venga lo que viniere, el lunes abrimos la librería.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Come what may, we open the bookshop on Monday.

vocabulary.term: adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres
vocabulary.meaning: when in Rome, do as the Romans do (lit. wherever you go, do what you see)
vocabulary.example: Aquí se cena a las diez: adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here people have dinner at ten: when in Rome, do as the Romans do.

vocabulary.meaning: he / she said to him / her (literary; today le dijo)
vocabulary.example: Díjole el notario que volviera al día siguiente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The notary told him to come back the next day.

vocabulary.meaning: once upon a time (érase = se era, there was)
vocabulary.example: Érase una vez un archivero que no tiraba ningún papel.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Once upon a time there was an archivist who never threw a single paper away.

vocabulary.meaning: on pain of, under penalty of
vocabulary.example: Deberá abonar la cuota antes del día quince, so pena de recargo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You must pay the fee before the fifteenth, on pain of a surcharge.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde, a la sazón notario del pueblo, firmó el acta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor, at that time the town notary, signed the record.

vocabulary.example: La otrora próspera fábrica es hoy un museo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The once-prosperous factory is now a museum.

vocabulary.meaning: the aforementioned (legal; often ironic in speech)
vocabulary.example: El susodicho no se presentó a la vista.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The aforementioned did not appear at the hearing.

quiz.prompt: Old statute: «El que ___ uso indebido del sello oficial será sancionado.» Which future subjunctive fits?
quiz.explanation: Legal texts use the future subjunctive for any case the law foresees: hicieron → hiciere. Hiciera is imperfect subjunctive and haría is conditional; neither fits a rule about the future.
hints: Take the preterite ellos form, remove -ron and add -re.

quiz.prompt: Modern Spanish for «Si no hubiere quórum, se aplaza la sesión»: Si no ___ quórum, se aplaza la sesión.
quiz.explanation: After si, the future subjunctive becomes a present indicative: si no hay quórum. Modern Spanish never uses si with the present subjunctive.
hints: After si, which mood does modern Spanish use?

quiz.prompt: Complete the set phrase with its fossil form: Sea lo que ___, firmaremos mañana.
quiz.explanation: The fixed phrase is sea lo que fuere (be that as it may), with the future subjunctive of ser; today people also say sea lo que sea.
hints: Start from the ellos preterite of ser and swap -ron for -re.

quiz.prompt: Which stem is the future subjunctive built on?
quiz.explanation: Like hablara and hablase, it takes the preterite ellos stem: hablaron → hablare, tuvieron → tuviere. The ordinary future (hablaré) is built on the infinitive instead.
hints: It shares its stem with hablara / hablase.

quiz.prompt: Rewrite in modern word order: «Díjole el juez que callase.» → ___ dijo el juez que callase.
quiz.explanation: A pronoun stuck to a finite verb (díjole) is a fossil of literary prose; today it goes in front: le dijo.
hints: Move the pronoun in front of the verb.

quiz.prompt: Complete the proverb: Adonde fueres, haz lo que ___.
quiz.explanation: Both halves are future subjunctive: fueres (from fueron) and vieres (from vieron). Modern sense: adonde vayas, haz lo que veas.
hints: Future subjunctive of ver, tú form.
Start from the ellos preterite of ver: -ron becomes -res.
teaches: adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres

quiz.prompt: «Deberá presentar el recibo antes del viernes, so pena de perder la plaza.» So pena de means…
quiz.explanation: So is the old preposition bajo (under): so pena de = under penalty of. Missing the deadline costs you the place.

quiz.prompt: «El ministro, a la sazón embajador en Lima, firmó el tratado.» A la sazón tells you that he was ambassador…
quiz.explanation: A la sazón = entonces, en aquel momento: he was ambassador when he signed.
hints: It places the fact in time.

quiz.prompt: In a modern work e-mail, «Si tuviere alguna duda, llámeme» is the natural choice.
quiz.explanation: The future subjunctive is for recognising, not producing. Today you write si tiene alguna duda; tuviere would sound like an old deed.
hints: Recognise it; do not produce it.

listening.text: Sea lo que fuere, cenamos aquí.
listening.meaning: Be that as it may, we're having dinner here.
listening.note: Sea lo que fuere = sea lo que sea.

listening.text: La otrora famosa posada está cerrada.
listening.meaning: The once-famous inn is closed.
listening.note: New word: la posada = the inn.

listening.text: Venga lo que viniere, no pienso rendirme.
listening.meaning: Come what may, I don't intend to give up.

listening.text: Díjole el capitán que no volviera sin noticias.
listening.meaning: The captain told him not to come back without news.

listening.text: Mi abuela, a la sazón maestra, vivía en Toledo.
listening.meaning: My grandmother, a teacher at the time, lived in Toledo.

listening.text: El reglamento prohíbe fumar en el patio, so pena de multa.
listening.meaning: The rules forbid smoking in the courtyard, on pain of a fine.
listening.note: New word: la multa = the fine.

listening.text: Si el inquilino no pagare la renta, el contrato quedará anulado.
listening.meaning: Should the tenant fail to pay the rent, the contract shall be void.
listening.note: Pagare without an accent is future subjunctive: read it as paga.

listening.text: Según la ley antigua, el que hallare un tesoro deberá avisar al ayuntamiento.
listening.meaning: Under the old law, whoever finds a treasure must inform the town hall.

guide.section: A future built on the preterite

guide.tip: If you meet a -re form you do not know, read it as a present: after si, the indicative (si hubiere → si hay); anywhere else, the subjunctive (el que hiciere → el que haga).

conversations.title: An old deed
conversations.scenario: Tomás has inherited his great-grandparents' house; his lawyer, Inés, reads him the deed of sale from nineteen twenty-eight.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Esta escritura de mil novecientos veintiocho está llena de fósiles gramaticales.
lines.meaning: This deed from nineteen twenty-eight is full of grammatical fossils.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ya lo veo. ¿Qué quiere decir «si el comprador no pagare en plazo»?
lines.meaning: So I see. What does 'si el comprador no pagare en plazo' mean?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pagare, sin tilde, es futuro de subjuntivo. Hoy diríamos: si el comprador no paga a tiempo.
lines.meaning: Pagare, without an accent, is future subjunctive. Today we'd say: if the buyer doesn't pay on time.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y lo de «so pena de perder la finca»?
lines.meaning: And the bit about 'so pena de perder la finca'?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Significa que, si no pagaba, perdería la finca. So es el antiguo bajo.
lines.meaning: It means that if he didn't pay, he would lose the property. So is the old word for bajo.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Aquí pone que el vendedor, a la sazón alcalde, firmó como testigo.
lines.meaning: It says here that the seller, at that time mayor, signed as a witness.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: A la sazón es entonces: cuando se firmó, él era el alcalde.
lines.meaning: A la sazón means then: when it was signed, he was the mayor.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y quién es ese susodicho que aparece en cada párrafo?
lines.meaning: And who is this 'aforementioned' who turns up in every paragraph?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: El propio comprador. Hoy pondríamos el citado comprador, o simplemente su nombre.
lines.meaning: The buyer himself. Today we'd write the said buyer, or simply his name.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues sea lo que fuere, la casa es de mi familia desde entonces.
lines.meaning: Well, be that as it may, the house has belonged to my family ever since.
lines.note: sea lo que fuere = sea lo que sea

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Exacto. Y tranquilo: nadie le pedirá que escriba así; basta con saber leerlo.
lines.meaning: Exactly. And don't worry: no one will ask you to write like that; it's enough to be able to read it.

bites.title: Built on the preterite
bites.rule: Take the preterite ellos form, drop -ron, add -re: hablaron → hablare, tuvieron → tuviere, fueron → fuere. Only nosotros has a written accent: habláremos.
bites.example: Si el inquilino no pagare, se rescindirá el contrato.
bites.example_meaning: Should the tenant fail to pay, the contract shall be terminated.

bites.title: Read it, don't write it
bites.rule: It lives in old laws, contracts and proverbs. Read it as a present: after si use the indicative (si hubiere → si hay); elsewhere use the subjunctive (el que hiciere → el que haga).
bites.example: Quien tuviere dudas → quien tenga dudas.

bites.title: Other fossils
bites.rule: Formal prose keeps other relics: pronouns stuck to the verb (díjole, érase), so pena de (on pain of), a la sazón (at that time), otrora (formerly), el susodicho.

sorts.title: Fossil or modern?
sorts.why: The fossil ends in -re on the preterite stem (hubie-, fue-, tuvie-, vinie-); the modern form is the present subjunctive.

sorts.title: Which modern equivalent?
sorts.why: After si, the fossil becomes a present indicative (si no hay, si no paga, si es necesario); in relative clauses and set phrases, a present subjunctive (el que haga, quien tenga, sea lo que sea).

spots.sentence: Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieras.
spots.why: Both halves of the proverb are future subjunctive: fueres… vieres.

spots.sentence: Si no haya acuerdo, decidirá el juez.
spots.why: Modern si takes the present indicative, never the present subjunctive: si no hay acuerdo.

spots.sentence: El testigo que hablaren sin permiso será amonestado.
spots.why: One witness, so the singular: el testigo que hablare.

spots.sentence: Deberá pagar antes del lunes, so pena por recargo.
spots.why: The formula is so pena de: under penalty of.

spots.sentence: Si el comprador no pagaré en plazo, perderá la finca.
spots.why: The future subjunctive has no written accent; pagaré is the ordinary future (and a promissory note).

builds.meaning: Be that as it may, we will sign.

builds.text: Venga lo que viniere, seguiremos adelante.
builds.meaning: Come what may, we will carry on.
The notary told him to wait.

builds.text: Si no hubiere acuerdo, decidirá el juez.
builds.meaning: Should there be no agreement, the judge shall decide.

realm.content:
## Fueros antiguos en Eldmark

The old charters of Highgate still speak in fossils: **el que hallare la espada la devolverá al rey**; **si el dragón despertare, sonarán las campanas**. Chroniclers like **díjole el enano**, **so pena de destierro** and **la otrora gloriosa Deepanvil**. Read each **-re** as a present: **el que halle**, **si despierta**.

vocabulary.example: Fuere orco o elfa, el viajero paga peaje en Highgate.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Be they orc or elf, the traveller pays a toll in Highgate.

vocabulary.example: Si hubiere dragón en la mazmorra, huid.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Should there be a dragon in the dungeon, flee.

vocabulary.example: Díjole la maga al paladín que guardara silencio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage told the paladin to keep quiet.

vocabulary.example: Nadie entra en el Bosque Umbrío de noche, so pena de destierro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: No one enters the Bosque Umbrío at night, on pain of exile.

vocabulary.example: La otrora orgullosa Deepanvil es hoy una mina vacía.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The once-proud Deepanvil is now an empty mine.

vocabulary.example: El susodicho minotauro no pagó la cerveza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The aforementioned minotaur did not pay for his beer.

vocabulary.meaning: charter, a town's ancient code of law
vocabulary.example: El fuero de Highgate data de tiempos remotos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Highgate's charter dates from ancient times.

vocabulary.example: El destierro del cazador duró siete inviernos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The hunter's exile lasted seven winters.

vocabulary.example: La cronista anota cada batalla con letra diminuta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The chronicler records every battle in tiny handwriting.

bites.title: Leyes de Highgate
bites.rule: Eldmark's charters use the future subjunctive for every case the law foresees: el que robare, si el rey muriere. Read it as a present: el que robe, si muere.
bites.example: Si el rey muriere sin heredero, reinará su hermana.
bites.example_meaning: Should the king die without an heir, his sister shall reign.

listening.text: Díjole el enano que siguiera.
listening.meaning: The dwarf told him to carry on.

listening.text: La otrora gloriosa Deepanvil duerme.
listening.meaning: Once-glorious Deepanvil sleeps.

listening.text: So pena de destierro, nadie cruza el puente.
listening.meaning: On pain of exile, no one crosses the bridge.

listening.text: El que hallare la corona la devolverá.
listening.meaning: Whoever finds the crown shall return it.

listening.text: La cronista escribió: sea lo que fuere, vencimos.
listening.meaning: The chronicler wrote: be that as it may, we won.
listening.note: New word: la cronista = the chronicler.

builds.text: Venga lo que viniere, el paladín resiste.
builds.meaning: Come what may, the paladin holds firm.
The elf told him to be quiet.

spots.sentence: El guerrero que robaren el botín será desterrado.
spots.why: One warrior, so the singular: el guerrero que robare.

spots.sentence: Si el dragón despertaré, sonarán las campanas.
spots.why: The future subjunctive has no written accent: despertare, not the future despertaré.

sorts.title: Fossil or modern in the chronicle?
sorts.why: Enclitics on finite verbs, the future subjunctive and otrora belong to old chronicles; the modern versions put the pronoun first, use the present and say antes.

quiz.prompt: Highgate charter: «Si hubiere dragón en la mazmorra, huid.» In modern Spanish: Si ___ dragón en la mazmorra, huid.
quiz.explanation: After si, the future subjunctive becomes a present indicative: si hay dragón.
hints: After si, modern Spanish uses the present indicative.

quiz.prompt: «Nadie entra en el Bosque Umbrío de noche, so pena de destierro.» So pena de destierro means…
quiz.explanation: So pena de = bajo pena de. Break the rule and you are banished.

meadowbrook.content:
## Refranes en Meadowbrook

The Meadowbrook almanac is full of old sayings: **el que plantare en invierno, cosechará poco**. The town bylaws still say **si la cosecha se perdiere, el alcalde perdonará el impuesto**. Rosa reads them aloud and translates on the spot: **si se pierde**. Nora shrugs and plants anyway: **venga lo que viniere**.

vocabulary.example: Venga lo que viniere, mañana plantamos maíz.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Come what may, tomorrow we plant corn.

vocabulary.example: Si hubiere helada, se taparán las fresas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Should there be a frost, the strawberries shall be covered.

vocabulary.example: Sea lo que fuere, la calabaza de Nora ganó el concurso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Be that as it may, Nora's pumpkin won the contest.

vocabulary.example: Leo, a la sazón aprendiz de pescador, encontró el almanaque en el río.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo, at that time an apprentice fisherman, found the almanac in the river.

vocabulary.example: La mina, otrora tranquila, está llena de visitantes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mine, once quiet, is full of visitors.

vocabulary.example: La susodicha vaca se comió las fresas del alcalde.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The aforementioned cow ate the mayor's strawberries.

vocabulary.example: El almanaque predice lluvia para la fiesta de otoño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The almanac predicts rain for the autumn festival.

vocabulary.example: Cada página del almanaque trae un refrán.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Every page of the almanac carries a saying.

vocabulary.example: La helada llegó antes de tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The frost came early.

bites.title: Refranes del almanaque
bites.rule: Old sayings keep the future subjunctive: el que plantare… cosechará. Read the -re form as a present: el que plante. You meet it in the almanac, rarely at Rosa's counter.
bites.example_meaning: Whoever rises early shall harvest first.

listening.text: El almanaque no miente.
listening.meaning: The almanac doesn't lie.
listening.note: New word: el almanaque = the almanac.

listening.text: Si hubiere helada, tapad las fresas.
listening.meaning: Should there be a frost, cover the strawberries.

listening.text: La susodicha gallina volvió a escaparse.
listening.meaning: The aforementioned hen got out again.

listening.text: El que cosechare tarde venderá barato.
listening.meaning: Whoever harvests late shall sell cheap.

listening.text: Leo, a la sazón pescador, vivía junto al río.
listening.meaning: Leo, a fisherman at the time, lived by the river.

builds.text: Sea lo que fuere, la vaca ganó.
builds.meaning: Be that as it may, the cow won.

builds.text: Díjole el alcalde a Nora que esperase.
builds.meaning: The mayor told Nora to wait.

spots.sentence: Si la cosecha se perdieré, el alcalde perdonará el impuesto.
spots.why: The future subjunctive has no written accent: perdiere.

spots.sentence: El que plantaren en invierno cosechará poco.
spots.why: El que is singular, so plantare.

sorts.title: Almanac or shop counter?
sorts.why: The almanac's -re forms sit on the preterite stem; at Rosa's counter people use the present subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: «Leo, a la sazón pescador, vivía junto al río.» This tells you that Leo…
options: was a fisherman at that time
quiz.correct_answer: was a fisherman at that time
quiz.explanation: A la sazón means then, at that time, whatever sazón (season, seasoning) suggests in the kitchen.
hints: It places the fact in time.

quiz.prompt: Modern version of the almanac's refrán: «El que cosechare tarde venderá barato» → El que ___ tarde venderá barato.
quiz.explanation: In a relative clause the fossil becomes a present subjunctive: el que coseche.
hints: A relative clause takes the present subjunctive.
-ar verbs take the opposite vowel, e, in the subjunctive.

conversations.title: The old bylaws
conversations.scenario: Nora brings the town's old bylaws to Rosa's seed shop and asks for a translation.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Rosa, ¿qué significa esto del reglamento: si la cosecha se perdiere?
lines.meaning: Rosa, what does this bit of the bylaws mean: si la cosecha se perdiere?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Es futuro de subjuntivo. Hoy diríamos: si se pierde la cosecha.
lines.meaning: It's future subjunctive. Today we'd say: if the harvest is lost.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y entonces el alcalde perdona el impuesto?
lines.meaning: And then the mayor waives the tax?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Eso dice. Aunque el susodicho alcalde no ha leído el reglamento en su vida.
lines.meaning: So it says. Although the aforementioned mayor has never read the bylaws in his life.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Aquí pone también: el que vendiere fresas sin permiso pagará una multa.
lines.meaning: It also says here: whoever sells strawberries without a permit shall pay a fine.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: O sea, el que venda fresas sin permiso. Tú lo tienes, tranquila.
lines.meaning: In other words, whoever sells strawberries without a permit. You've got one, don't worry.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Menos mal. Sea lo que fuere, este año pienso plantar el doble.
lines.meaning: Thank goodness. Be that as it may, this year I'm planning to plant twice as much.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues venga lo que viniere, aquí tendrás semillas.
lines.meaning: Well, come what may, you'll have seeds here.

rustwake.content:
## Bandos en el páramo

The Dome's old rulebook, read out on Radio Páramo, sounds like a notary: **el que saliere de la cúpula sin permiso perderá sus tuercas**; **si hubiere tormenta de ceniza, nadie abrirá la puerta**. The capataz Ruiz translates: **el que salga**, **si hay tormenta**. Old-timers still say **otrora** for the days before the Dome.

vocabulary.example: Si hubiere radiación, beba un tónico.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Should there be radiation, drink a tonic.

vocabulary.example: Quien tuviere agua filtrada deberá compartirla.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Whoever has filtered water must share it.

vocabulary.example: Prohibido tocar la antena, so pena de multa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Touching the antenna is forbidden, on pain of a fine.

vocabulary.example: El otrora brillante centro comercial está en ruinas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The once-gleaming shopping centre lies in ruins.

vocabulary.example: El susodicho escarabajo gigante volvió al taller.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The aforementioned giant beetle came back to the workshop.

vocabulary.example: Venga lo que viniere, la radio sigue emitiendo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Come what may, the radio stays on the air.

vocabulary.example: El capataz leyó el bando por la radio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The foreman read the proclamation over the radio.

vocabulary.example: El reglamento de la cúpula tiene cien páginas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The Dome's rulebook runs to a hundred pages.

vocabulary.example: La multa es de cien tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The fine is a hundred nuts.

bites.title: Bandos de la cúpula
bites.rule: The Dome's rulebook is written like an old law: el que saliere, si hubiere. Read each -re form as a present: el que salga, si hay.
bites.example: El que reparare la antena recibirá diez tuercas.
bites.example_meaning: Whoever repairs the antenna shall receive ten nuts.

listening.text: Venga lo que viniere, seguimos emitiendo.
listening.meaning: Come what may, we stay on the air.

listening.text: Si hubiere polvo, cerrad las ventanas.
listening.meaning: Should there be dust, shut the windows.
listening.note: Si hubiere reads as si hay.

listening.text: El bando prohíbe salir de noche.
listening.meaning: The proclamation forbids going out at night.
listening.note: New word: el bando = public notice.

listening.text: La otrora brillante gasolinera es hoy un mercado.
listening.meaning: The once-gleaming petrol station is now a market.

listening.text: El que hallare un disco lo traerá al taller.
listening.meaning: Whoever finds a disc shall bring it to the workshop.

builds.text: El que saliere perderá sus tuercas.
builds.meaning: Whoever goes out shall lose their nuts.
Should there be a storm, nobody goes out.

spots.sentence: El buscador que salieren sin permiso perderá sus tuercas.
spots.why: One scavenger, so the singular: el buscador que saliere.

spots.sentence: Prohibido tocar la antena, so pena en multa.
spots.why: The formula is so pena de.

sorts.title: Rulebook or radio chat?
sorts.why: The rulebook keeps the future subjunctive and otrora; on the radio people say el que salga, si hay and antes.

quiz.prompt: Radio bulletin: «Quien tuviere agua filtrada deberá compartirla.» The modern version is…
options: Quien tenga agua filtrada deberá compartirla.
Quien tendrá agua filtrada deberá compartirla.
Quien tuviera agua filtrada deberá compartirla.
quiz.correct_answer: Quien tenga agua filtrada deberá compartirla.
quiz.explanation: In a relative clause about the future, the fossil becomes a present subjunctive: quien tenga.
hints: A relative clause takes the present subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: From the Dome's rulebook: Prohibido tocar la antena, so pena ___ multa.
quiz.explanation: The fixed formula is so pena de: under penalty of.
hints: The same preposition as in bajo pena ___.
